title: Breath of the Wild Was Prototyped as an NES Game
hook:
Breath of the Wild's first prototype looked like the 1986 NES Zelda. Nintendo built it just to test setting trees on fire. Which Zelda did you play first?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Breath of the Wild was first built as an eight bit game? Before the giant open world existed, the team made a prototype that looked like the original 1986 Zelda on the NES. Director Hidemaro Fujibayashi showed it at the Game Developers Conference in March 2017, in a talk called Change and Constant. The tiny prototype existed to test one big idea. Nintendo called it the chemistry engine. Water, fire, wind and electricity could all affect the objects around Link. In one short clip, Fujibayashi fired an arrow through a campfire. The arrow caught fire and set a tree burning. That is the exact trick you can pull off in the finished game. The prototype also let the team try cutting down trees for lumber and setting whole fields on fire. Those experiments became the core of the final design. The developers said they looked at the boundaries of earlier Zelda games and designed around them. Once the prototype worked, the team scaled the idea up into a map with no invisible walls. Breath of the Wild launched on March 3, 2017, just days after that talk. The biggest Zelda ever made started out as the smallest. Follow for more gaming history.
